\documentclass[11pt]{article}\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}\usepackage{amsmath,amsthm}\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}\newtheorem{remark}{Remark}
\title{Normalized Transfer of a Nonlinear Dispersion Tail}\author{}\date{21 July 2026}\begin{document}\maketitle
\begin{abstract}We give the exact event-inclusion and normalized-measure theorem transporting the dependent Gaussian dispersion tail to a convex nonlinear $SU(2)$ chart.\end{abstract}
Let $G$ be the local cylinder, let $D$ be nonlinear Fr\'echet dispersion, and let $Q$ be the centered linear dispersion. Suppose each staple logarithm has Taylor remainder at most $\epsilon$, the metric factor is $s_r$, and
\[\mu(A\cap G)\le e^\ell\nu(A\cap G),\qquad \mu(G^c)\le q_{\rm exc}.\]
\begin{theorem}For $m$ staples and $\eta>0$,
\[\{D\ge m\eta^2\}\cap G\subseteq\{Q\ge m(s_r\eta-\epsilon)_+^2\},\]
and therefore
\[\mu\{D\ge m\eta^2\}\le e^\ell\nu\{Q\ge m(s_r\eta-\epsilon)_+^2\}+q_{\rm exc}.\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}Stage 41 gives $P\ge s_r^2D$. Centering is a contraction, so the staple Taylor remainder gives $\sqrt P\le\sqrt Q+\sqrt m\epsilon$. Rearrangement proves the inclusion. Split the event over $G$ and $G^c$ and apply the two normalized premises.\end{proof}
At nonlinear RMS threshold $0.006$, the frozen centered reference meets the allocated high-channel budget after chart loss.
\begin{remark}The density and complement premises have not been proved uniformly over physical retained boundary states; the numerical closure is restricted.\end{remark}\end{document}
